items.followUp: State the law of inertia and explain what inertia means.

rubric.why: The law states that a body maintains its state of rest or uniform motion.
rubric.description: States the unchanged state of rest or motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform motion.

rubric.why: The law specifies that an external force is required to change that state.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the state changes only when an external force acts.

modelAnswer: A body remains at rest or continues to move with uniform velocity in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
This tendency of a body to resist a change in its state of rest or motion is called inertia.

items.followUp: Define power and state how many joules per second are equal to one watt.

rubric.why: Power describes how quickly work is done.
rubric.description: Defines power as the rate of doing work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or the relation between power, work and time.

rubric.why: One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating 1 W = 1 J/s or its equivalent in words.

modelAnswer: Power is the rate of doing work.
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.

items.followUp: A lamp hangs at rest from two vertical strings with tensions of 5.2 N and 6.1 N. Find its weight.

rubric.why: Both given tensions are needed to find the total upward force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating both tension values with units.

rubric.why: At rest, the frame is in equilibrium and its weight balances the upward tensions.
rubric.description: Relates the weight to the total tension using equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the weight equals the sum of the tensions.

rubric.why: This is the force-balance equation for the hanging frame.
rubric.description: Writes the equation for the weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation.

rubric.why: Both tension values must be substituted into the equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution.

rubric.why: The weight is the sum of the two tensions, stated as a force.
rubric.description: Gives the calculated weight with its unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Since the picture frame is at rest, it is in equilibrium.
